messages:
maria: FYI — Crestline POC kickoff tomorrow. They want a 4wk POC for two flows: 1) support ticket triage (intent + entity extraction) 2) merchant order summarization. Need a prompt inventory, baseline prompts + small eval plan and a rough cost/latency target we can present to them. @sam_se @lee_ml can you help scope acceptance criteria?

sam_se: Got it. Do we have a sample data snapshot and expected QPS for the POC? That drives model choice and latency targets.

maria: They provided 5k anonymized tickets + 2k merchant orders. Expect ~10 reqs/sec peak during demo. They prefer hosted API but will accept Dedicated if needed. Also will ask about PII handling in security questionnaire.

lee_ml: Quick thoughts: baseline plan — start with a small prompt set and labeled eval of ~200 examples per flow. Metrics: intent classification acc >= 92%, entity extraction F1 >= 0.90, summary ROUGE-L > 0.45 or judged as "actionable" in spot checks. Perf: p95 latency < 250ms for triage single-turn on a 13B quantized variant; fallback to 7B if cost > target.

chandra: Security note: Crestline will require answers on PII handling. For the hosted POC recommend we pseudonymize customer names and account IDs before sending. If they insist on raw data, propose Dedicated or Private. Also list of controls they may ask: KMS, retention settings, audit logs.

sam_se: Prompt inventory idea — capture canonical user messages and edge cases, then build 3 prompt tiers: baseline (short), safety-filter (explicit constraints), and high-precision (few-shot examples). Example baseline prompt for triage:```
System: You are an assistant that assigns an intent tag and extracts key entities from support tickets.
User: "{ticket_text}"
Assistant: Provide JSON with keys: {"intent": "<one of: billing, technical, account, other>", "entities": [{"type":"<email|order_id|product>", "text":"..."}], "confidence": 0.0} 
```
Keep model instructions minimal for latency.

maria: Nice. Can we get a concrete eval harness? I want something we can run end-to-end and share in the POC report.

lee_ml: I can produce an eval harness with 200 labeled triage tickets and 200 orders. We'll compute classification accuracy, entity F1, and a small human review for summarization quality (10 blind samples scored 0-3). I'll hook it into an evals.yaml that calls the Redwood API and logs per-prompt token cost.

sam_se: Cost targets — Crestline asked for predictable demo spend. Propose we quote: hosted POC estimate $300–$600 for the 4wk run (includes 5k tickets + 2k orders at expected sample rates), with per-1k-token estimate surfaced in the report. If Dedicated required, we give reserved capacity pricing.

chandra: Add legal note: get DPA signed before we ingest any customer PII. For now treat demo data as sanitized. Also confirm retention window set to 30 days and logs masked.

maria: Timeline proposal — week 0 (prep) prompt inventory + baseline prompts; week1 integrate baseline + run eval harness; week2 iterate prompts and run performance tests; week3 integrate to demo flows & create report; week4 acceptance & handoff. Can we commit to printing the POC report by EOW week3?

lee_ml: Yes — I’ll deliver initial eval results by end of week1 and a short report end of week3.

sam_se: I'll prepare the pricing slide and include fallback options (7B for cost, Dedicated for SLA). Also will draft a short runbook for demo ops (how to throttle, switch model, logs).

devops-bot: Reminder: if we need Dedicated infra, open a capacity request at least 5 business days before the demo.

maria: Great — next steps: @lee_ml share eval harness link, @sam_se price slide, @chandra security checklist. Will sync tomorrow 10:30am. :thumbsup:
